title: covered_by_grant no longer matches relocated grants; invocation cwd is dropped (0.1.2+), breaks errand's /workspace
body:
## Summary

`covered_by_grant()` no longer matches a **relocated grant** against the invocation directory, so the working directory is dropped to the private home. This breaks `QaidVoid/errand`, which starts its sandbox with cwd = the host project path and relocates that path to `/workspace`.

Introduced in the 0.1.2 cycle; still present in 0.1.3.

## Repro

Policy (relocated grant for the project and the state dir):

```toml
[filesystem]
reset = true
read = ["/usr", "/lib", "/lib64", "/bin", "/sbin", "/proc",
        { path = "/tmp/reloc-proj", at = "/workspace" },
        { path = "/tmp/reloc-state", at = "/state" }]
write = [{ path = "/tmp/reloc-proj", at = "/workspace" },
         { path = "/tmp/reloc-state", at = "/state" }]
execute = ["/usr", "/lib", "/lib64", "/bin", "/sbin", "/state/home/bin"]

[env]
pass = []
set = { PATH = "/state/home/bin:/usr/bin:/bin", HOME = "/state/home" }

[resources]
file_max = "1g"

[network]
egress_allow = [{ host = "*", port = 443 }]
```

Run with the invocation directory set to the grant's source path:

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/reloc-proj /tmp/reloc-state
bailey trust /tmp/reloc.toml
(cd /tmp/reloc-proj && bailey run --config /tmp/reloc.toml /bin/sh -c 'echo PWD=$(pwd)')
```

Expected (bailey 0.1.0 / 0.1.1):

```
PWD=/workspace
```

Actual (bailey 0.1.2 / 0.1.3):

```
bailey: warning: the working directory is not granted, so it is absent under
isolation; starting in the private home instead (/…/bailey/<target>/home).
Grant the directory to keep it.
PWD=/home/samuel
```

## Root cause

`crates/bailey/src/backend/world.rs`, `fn covered_by_grant`:

- **0.1.0 / 0.1.1** matched each grant against `rule.path` (the source path):
  ```rust
  .map(|rule| &rule.path)
  ```
  A relocated grant `{ path: H, at: "/workspace" }` therefore covers the host cwd `H` -> `kept_invocation_dir = true` -> `relocated_dir()` maps the cwd to `/workspace`.

- **0.1.2 / 0.1.3** match against `rule.at.unwrap_or(&rule.path)` (the placement path):
  ```rust
  .map(|rule| rule.at.as_ref().unwrap_or(&rule.path))
  ```
  The grant is now treated as covering `/workspace`, which the host cwd `H` never `starts_with` -> `kept_invocation_dir = false` -> cwd falls back to the private home.

Because `kept_invocation_dir` is false, the branch documented in `world.rs` (~lines 112-119, "A relocated grant does not exist at its host path inside the sandbox, so the directory to enter is where the grant was placed") is unreachable for relocated grants.

Adding a *direct* grant of the host path alongside the relocated grant does not help on 0.1.3, which confirms this is the matching semantics, not a missing grant.

## Suggested fix

Treat a grant as covering both its source path and its placement path:

```rust
fn covered_by_grant(policy: &Policy, path: &Path) -> bool {
    policy
        .filesystem
        .iter()
        .flat_map(|rule| [rule.path.as_path(), rule.at.as_deref()].into_iter().flatten())
        .chain(policy.devices.iter().map(|rule| rule.path.as_path()))
        .any(|granted| path.starts_with(granted))
}
```

## Impact

- errand (`QaidVoid/errand`) starts its confined agent with cwd = the host project path and relocates it to `/workspace`; with bailey 0.1.2+ the agent starts in a private home instead, so it no longer works in the project directory.
- Because of this, errand cannot adopt bailey 0.1.3 today, which is the release containing the btrfs-ioctl Landlock-bypass fix — so the regression also blocks the security fix from being deployed.
